summary: Toussus-le-Noble Airport is a historic general aviation airfield located in the Yvelines department, about 20 km southwest of Paris. Established in the early 20th century, it primarily serves business aviation, flight training, and private pilots rather than scheduled commercial flights. The airport remains one of the busiest general aviation fields in the Paris region, featuring multiple FBOs and flight schools.
faqs:
Q: Does Toussus-le-Noble Airport have commercial passenger flights?
A: No, TNF is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial service. It caters mainly to private, business, and training flights.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport hosts several FBOs, flight schools, aircraft maintenance services, fueling facilities, and restaurants on site.

Q: How far is it from central Paris?
A: It is roughly 20 km (12 miles) southwest of central Paris, typically a 30-45 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Can I visit the airport as a spectator?
A: The airport has public areas and viewing points, making it popular among aviation enthusiasts, though secure zones are restricted.
transport_tips: The most practical way to reach Toussus-le-Noble is by car via the A10 or A86 motorways, with on-site parking available near the terminals. A taxi or private transfer from Paris typically takes 30-45 minutes depending on traffic. Public transport options are limited, so renting a car or arranging a transfer is recommended for travelers.
local_tip: If you're picking someone up or being picked up, coordinate timing carefully—the small terminal area can get crowded during peak flight school hours (mornings and late afternoons), and parking right at the terminal fills up fast. Locals often use the overflow lot and walk over.
